title: DNA Mechanical Strain Steers Transcription Factor Recognition.
authors: Afek, Ariel; Yao, Minyi; O'Hagan, Michael; Onoon, Karn; Givon, Lihee; Rogotner, Shelly; Salinas, Raul; Nithun, Raj; Kessler, Naama; Jbara, Muhammad; Dym, Orly; Pipatpolkai, Tanadet; Schumacher, Maria
one_liner_zh: 该文通过高通量平台PIC-NIC系统研究DNA骨架力学扰动对15种转录因子结合的影响，结合结构、动力学和分子模拟揭示力学敏感位点与应变适应几何构象的互作机制，高度契合TF-DNA互作与物理模拟方法课题。
abstract: DNA is not merely a linear code of bases, but a mechanically constrained polymer whose backbone continuity restricts the conformations accessible during protein recognition. Yet, although base-sequence preferences have been extensively mapped across human transcription factor (TF) families, we lack comparable maps of how TFs read backbone continuity and DNA mechanics, leaving these layers of recognition poorly understood. Here we introduce PIC-NIC, a high-throughput platform that uses site-specific backbone nicks to perturb DNA mechanics while preserving base identity and minimizing accompanying chemical changes. Across 15 TFs spanning eight structural families, PIC-NIC reveals a highly position-dependent response to backbone disruption: most positions are permissive, whereas nicking at mechanically sensitive sites can substantially reshape binding. Mechanistic analyses integrating PIC-NIC maps with newly determined TF-DNA structures, structural comparisons, binding kinetics, and molecular simulations show that sensitive positions often coincide with strain-adapted DNA geometries, including Hoogsteen conformations, whose relaxation can enhance binding or rewire sequence specificity. Genomic single-strand breaks and repair maps further suggest that TF retention at nicked DNA may influence local repair-factor accessibility. Together, these findings systematically map DNA backbone mechanics as a position-resolved layer of TF recognition across diverse protein families, showing how this layer can reshape binding specificity and may influence repair-factor accessibility.
abstract_zh: DNA并非仅仅是碱基的线性编码，而是一种受机械约束的聚合物，其骨架连续性限制了蛋白质识别过程中可及的构象。然而，尽管碱基序列偏好已在人类转录因子（TF）家族中广泛绘制，我们仍缺乏TF如何读取骨架连续性和DNA力学的可比图谱，导致这些识别层面仍知之甚少。在此，我们引入PIC-NIC，一种高通量平台，利用位点特异性骨架切口扰动DNA力学，同时保持碱基身份并最小化伴随的化学变化。跨越八个结构家族的15个TF中，PIC-NIC揭示了对骨架破坏的高度位置依赖性响应：大多数位置是容许的，而机械敏感位点的切口可显著重塑结合。整合PIC-NIC图谱与新确定的TF-DNA结构、结构比较、结合动力学和分子模拟的机制分析表明，敏感位置常与应变适应的DNA几何构象（包括Hoogsteen构象）重合，其松弛可增强结合或重编程序列特异性。基因组单链断裂和修复图谱进一步提示，切口DNA上的TF滞留可能影响局部修复因子的可及性。综合来看，这些发现系统性地将DNA骨架力学绘制为跨多样蛋白家族的TF识别位置分辨层面，展示该层面如何重塑结合特异性并可能影响修复因子的可及性。
